pairs.why: Both match the painted style, but A's logs and stones look slightly more matte and grounded, while B's logs glow a little more glossily.
B's log glow and shading are slightly calmer and more painterly, closer to the real campfire under the pot; A's logs look a bit plastic and over-lit.
B builds a more believable crossed-log teepee with clearly cut ends, while A's logs look slightly rubbery and toy-like.
A's crossed logs with readable cut ends and its softer kettle read a bit more like a built object with the real cards' moderate finish.
A's flame and logs are painted with softer, less glossy light, closer to the real cards; B's logs glow more strongly and look plastic.
B has a more restrained glow and a cleaner teepee build, while A's bright glowing log ends push toward a glossy toy look.
The two are nearly the same; A's logs and stone ring are marginally more solid and less glowy.
B's logs and flame are slightly softer and more matte, closer to the real cards' smooth but not glossy finish.
